headline: DeepSeek has reportedly doubled its second funding round to about 100 billion yuan while keeping its valuation at around 500 billion yuan.
score_reason: Lowered one point from the pool score: the figures come from unnamed mainland media relayed by one Hong Kong outlet, the round is described as nearing completion, and DeepSeek has not confirmed it.
importance_line: A round this size would be the largest private financing in China this year by the report's account, and would move one of the country's best-known AI developers toward a stock-market listing, but the round is described as nearing completion, not closed, and DeepSeek has not confirmed the figures.
summary: The Standard of Hong Kong reports, citing mainland Chinese media it does not name, that DeepSeek is nearing the end of a second funding round that has doubled to 100 billion yuan (about HK$117 billion) in half a month, at an unchanged pre-money valuation (the company's worth before the new money goes in) of about 500 billion yuan, with the battery maker CATL planning another 10 billion yuan and the carmaker Geely among the new investors. If it closes, DeepSeek will have raised 150 billion yuan in six months, which the report calls China's largest primary-market financing this year, and it is expected to restructure and prepare a stock-market listing on the Science and Technology Innovation Board; Bloomberg separately reported that DeepSeek is leading a seed round for the robotics start-up Winverse AI.
notes: Read in full via fulltext. Source credit kept to The Standard, which names no original outlet.
